program_name: Medicine and Surgery (MedInTO) - One Long-Cycle Degree Programme in Medicine and Surgery / Medicina e Chirurgia in lingua inglese
teaching_language: Fully English-taught (case 1). The whole 6-year, 360-ECTS single-cycle degree is delivered in English at UNITO's Orbassano site; apply.unito.it lists 'Study language: English' and the en.unito.it degree record (course code 1901U62) lists 'Language: English'. It is a single UNITO degree (not an interuniversity/joint degree) and not an English pathway inside an Italian-named curriculum - the Italian-language Medicina e Chirurgia degrees at Torino and Orbassano are separate programmes with their own admission calls. Note: although teaching is in English, the programme requires Italian at B2 level before students can start curricular clinical clerkships from year 3 (patient contact); the Italian requirement is deemed satisfied by passing the courses SCB0562 English and Italian Medical Language and SCB0565 Clinical Language.
campus: Orbassano (Turin metropolitan area), Piedmont, Italy - San Luigi Gonzaga University Hospital campus, Regione Gonzole 10. Administering unit: Department of Clinical and Biological Sciences (Dipartimento di Scienze Cliniche e Biologiche). Not the central Turin city campus.
degree_class: LM-41 R - Medicina e chirurgia (Italian single-cycle master's degree class LM-41, Medicine and Surgery). UNITO internal course code: 1901U62.
admission_type: Restricted access - nationally programmed number of places (accesso programmato a livello nazionale) regulated by Ministerial Decree. Admission is decided exclusively by a national entrance test (IMAT-type exam) governed by MUR Ministerial Decree No. 1005 of 6 August 2026 for a.y. 2026/2027; no TOLC, no SAT, no portfolio/interview. Registration for the test is done on the ministerial Universitaly portal (www.universitaly.it), NOT via Apply@UniTo: the UNITO admission call states explicitly that candidates holding a foreign entry qualification must NOT submit a preliminary application on the Apply@UniTo platform for this programme. Consistent with this, the apply.unito.it course page for Medicine and Surgery currently shows 'Not available for applying at the moment'. Candidates additionally have to complete a pre-enrolment step inside MyUniTo (Pre-iscrizioni ad accesso programmato). EU/equivalent candidates compete in a national merit ranking; non-EU candidates residing abroad compete only in a separate local UNITO ranking. Note: the en.unito.it degree-record summary box labels Access as 'Local programmed', which conflicts with the admission call and the same page's own descriptive text ('accesso programmato nazionale' / 'fixed quota of places decided by a ministerial order') - the national-programmed classification from the official call should be considered authoritative.
application_deadline_eu: A.y. 2026/2027: registration for the admission test on the Universitaly portal from 26 August 2026 until 9 September 2026, 15:00 (GMT+2) - this is also the final deadline to set/confirm the irrevocable order of university preferences. Entrance test on 29 September 2026. National merit rankings published in the Universitaly reserved area on 26 October 2026. After being assigned/booked ('assegnato'/'prenotato') in a ranking, candidates must confirm enrolment and pay the first instalment within a maximum of 4 working days (including the day of the ranking release, excluding Saturdays and public holidays), by 15:00 Italian time. Candidates with a foreign entry qualification do NOT use the Apply@UniTo application windows for this programme.
application_deadline_non_eu: A.y. 2026/2027 (non-EU citizens residing abroad and requiring a study visa, and Chinese 'Marco Polo' candidates): the same Universitaly test registration window applies (26 August 2026 to 9 September 2026, 15:00 GMT+2). In addition, the Universitaly visa pre-enrolment application must be submitted by 11 September 2026 - a Medicine-and-Surgery-in-English-specific extension of UNITO's general non-EU pre-enrolment deadline of 15 July 2026 (the Italian-taught 'Semestre Aperto' medicine/dentistry/veterinary deadline is 31 August 2026). Non-EU candidates residing abroad who chose UNITO as first preference must also complete the UniTo portal pre-enrolment (MyUniTo > Pre-iscrizioni ad accesso programmato > 'MEDICINE AND SURGERY - reserved to extra-EU applicants residing abroad requiring a study visa / Chinese students currently attending Marco Polo program') between 26 August 2026 and 11 September 2026, 15:00 (GMT+2). Marco Polo 2026/2027 candidates who already pre-enrolled on Universitaly in 2025 do not have to re-apply on Universitaly. The publication schedule and enrolment timing of the separate local UNITO ranking for non-EU applicants residing abroad is announced on the UniTo portal. [uncertain]
entry_exam_or_test: IMAT-type national admission test (prova di ammissione) for English-taught Medicine and Surgery, identical in content at all Italian and international test venues, governed by MUR Ministerial Decree No. 1005 of 6 August 2026. Date for a.y. 2026/2027: Tuesday 29 September 2026 (corrected by a MUR errata corrige from the originally announced 30 September 2026); in Italian venues the test starts at 13:30 and lasts 100 minutes. Structure: 60 multiple-choice questions with 5 options each - 4 reading skills and acquired knowledge, 5 logical reasoning and problems, 23 biology, 15 chemistry, 13 physics and mathematics. All questions are set in English. Scoring: maximum 90 points; +1.5 per correct answer, -0.4 per wrong answer, 0 for omitted. Eligibility thresholds: EU candidates and non-EU candidates covered by art. 39(5) of Legislative Decree 286/1998 must score at least 20 points to enter the ranking; for non-EU candidates residing abroad the 20-point threshold does not apply and any score above zero is eligible (candidates who answered no question at all are excluded). Tie-breaking order: (a) higher sub-scores in biology, then chemistry, then physics and mathematics, then logical reasoning, then reading/acquired knowledge; (b) possession, by the registration deadline, of one of the language certifications listed in Annex 3 to MD 1005/2026 as declared at test registration; (c) disability of 66% or more / disability under art. 3(3) of Law 104/1992; (d) younger candidate. Results calendar: 8 October 2026 anonymous score by label code on Universitaly, 19 October 2026 access to own test paper and score, 26 October 2026 national nominal rankings. No separate interview, motivation letter, or additional university-level test is used for admission. The admission test also serves as the check of minimum entry knowledge: weaknesses trigger Additional Learning Requirements (OFA / 'Additional Learning Obligations - ALO') to be cleared in the first year.
academic_requirements: Entry qualification: an Italian upper-secondary school diploma (diploma di scuola secondaria superiore) or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised as suitable under Italian law. UNITO's general rules for foreign qualifications require: (1) the diploma must give access to a university programme of the same level in the country of issue; (2) it must be obtained after at least 12 years of global schooling (EQF level 4 / ISCED 3) with at least the last two years attended in that same foreign education system. Holders of a diploma obtained after 10 or 11 years of schooling must supplement it with (a) one or two completed years of university studies with all first-year (or first two years') exams passed, or (b) a post-secondary qualification from a non-university higher institution in a related field, or (c) a Foundation Programme; example countries with fewer than 12 years include Azerbaijan, Brazil (pre-2006 qualifications), Colombia, Venezuela, Russia, Belarus, Peru, Kazakhstan, Ukraine and Costa Rica. Where a mandatory national university-entrance examination exists in the applicant's country (e.g. Greece, People's Republic of China, Republic of Cyprus, Spain), the same exam is also required for admission to the Italian university and must be documented. No bachelor's degree, GPA threshold, work experience or portfolio is required - selection is purely by IMAT-type test score within the quota. PLACES for a.y. 2026/2027 (definitive, set by MD No. 1005 of 6 August 2026 and confirmed by UNITO's supplementary notice): 105 places in total at UNITO - Orbassano, split into 73 places for EU candidates and non-EU candidates covered by art. 39(5) of Legislative Decree 286/1998 (i.e. non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy), 30 places for non-EU candidates residing abroad and requiring a visa, and 2 places for Chinese candidates in the 'Marco Polo' Programme. (The original UNITO call of 4 August 2026, published before MD 1005, listed provisional figures of 70 + 30 + 2 = 102; the 105/73/30/2 figures in the supplementary notice supersede them.) Passing the test and being ranked in an eligible position does not by itself guarantee enrolment: the International Students Section must first assess the foreign qualification, and only then is payment of the first instalment enabled. Successful candidates must also submit mandatory health certification for enrolment (see required_documents).
language_requirements: English: knowledge of English at CEFR level B2 or above is required of admitted students. The check of English knowledge and competence at B2 level is deemed to have been carried out through the admission test itself (which is written entirely in English) - there is no separate mandatory English certificate as an eligibility condition. If the lecturer in charge of the English and Italian Medical Language (EIML) course finds a student's English is below B2, the student is assigned an Additional Learning Requirement (OFA / ALO) that must be cleared before the first-year EIML exam; failure to clear it is handled through further activities and assessments specified on the programme website. Holding one of the language certifications listed in Annex 3 to MD No. 1005/2026, declared at test registration, is used only as a tie-break criterion in the ranking, not as an admission requirement. Italian: no Italian language requirement at admission for this English-taught programme (the CLIQ/CISIA ITA-L2 Italian B2 certificate that UNITO requires from non-EU visa applicants applies to Italian-taught free-access programmes, not to this one). However, an Italian level of B2 is required in order to access the curricular clinical clerkship activities from year 3 onwards, which involve patient contact; this Italian requirement is considered satisfied for students who have passed SCB0562 English and Italian Medical Language and SCB0565 Clinical Language. Documents submitted for the qualification assessment are accepted in Italian, English, French or Spanish; otherwise a certified translation into one of these languages is required. [uncertain]
required_documents: For test registration (all candidates, on Universitaly): online registration form with the irrevocable, ranked list of preferred universities/courses, declaration of any recognised language certification (Annex 3 to MD 1005/2026), and payment of the test fee. On test day: a valid identity document under Presidential Decree 445/2000 (identity card, passport, driving licence or equivalent photo ID issued by a State administration) and, for non-EU candidates, a valid residence permit or the receipt of its application, plus a copy of the receipt of payment of the admission-test contribution. For non-EU citizens residing abroad and requiring a visa: the Universitaly pre-enrolment (visa) application, submitted to UNITO as the chosen university, by 11 September 2026; plus UniTo portal registration and the MyUniTo pre-enrolment to the dedicated competition. For assessment of a foreign entry qualification by the International Students Section (requested by email from internationalstudents@unito.it to candidates ranked in an eligible position): valid ID card (EU/equivalent) or valid passport (non-EU); a residence permit valid for university enrolment for non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy under art. 39(5) of Legislative Decree 286/1998; the upper-secondary study qualification obtained after at least 12 years of global schooling, with proof of authenticity (legalisation, Apostille, ENIC-NARIC statement of verification, or an accepted national digital verification platform - such platforms exist for e.g. Turkey, India, Pakistan, Ukraine); transcript of records where there is any doubt about the years of schooling; the mandatory national entrance examination result with proof of authenticity where such an exam exists in the applicant's country; country-specific additional requirements; and optionally a declaration of value or a CIMEA statement of comparability (not mandatory but useful, and may be made mandatory at the office's discretion). If the applicant has not yet graduated at the time of application: an official certificate of enrolment in the final year stating the curriculum and the qualification to be obtained, plus an official score report for the years/semesters completed so far - the final qualification must be held in order to enrol. Documents must be signed/sealed/stamped; unsigned documents are refused, and incomplete files are not considered. For enrolment (matriculation) after assignment in the ranking: online confirmation of enrolment, a passport-style photograph, an identity document, the Italian fiscal code (codice fiscale), the printed and signed enrolment application, and the receipt of payment of the first instalment of university contributions via pagoPA in MyUniTo, all within 4 working days. For first-year students, mandatory health certification must also be uploaded: a copy of the vaccination certificate with legalisation (or Apostille) where applicable and an official Italian translation unless issued in English - covering at minimum the vaccinations compulsory in Italy (polio, diphtheria, tetanus, hepatitis B, measles, rubella) - and a certificate of a Mantoux tuberculin test performed at the local ASL or the competent health authority of the country of residence, or alternatively a lymphocyte stimulation / QuantiFERON test report. If not yet available at enrolment, a substitutive declaration undertaking to provide the documents within 30 days must be uploaded. Candidates with a disability or a specific learning disorder (DSA) who need aids or extra time must email their certification to ufficio.disabili@unito.it by the test registration deadline. Note: for this programme, candidates with a foreign qualification must NOT submit a preliminary application through Apply@UniTo.

uncertainty_notes:
SOURCE ACCESS PROBLEMS. (1) The programme's own microsite www.medinto.unito.it (IP 130.186.3.24) was completely unreachable during this research on 1 September 2026 - direct HTTPS requests returned connection refused or timed out from several different network paths, and a headless-browser reader also timed out. The MedInTO-specific statements above (B2 English wording, IMAT description, 'Additional Learning Obligations/ALO') therefore rest on search-engine indexed snippets of medinto.unito.it pages rather than on a live read of those pages, and should be re-verified once the microsite is back online. (2) en.unito.it, www.unito.it and apply.unito.it/courses/search returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to direct requests; the en.unito.it content used here was retrieved through a page-rendering reader proxy, so it is the official UNITO content but was not read directly. www.medicina.unito.it returned HTTP 405 to every request, so the older 2022/23 MedInTO IMAT call PDF hosted there could not be opened. The UNITO legal notice board (webapps.unito.it/albo_ateneo) and apply.unito.it/en_GB/courses/course/462 were reachable directly and are the strongest first-hand sources used.

SUBSTANTIVE UNCERTAINTIES. (a) Number of places: the UNITO admission call of 4 August 2026 gives provisional figures of 70 EU/non-EU-resident-in-Italy + 30 non-EU abroad + 2 Marco Polo = 102, while the supplementary notice issued after MD No. 1005 of 6 August 2026 gives definitive figures of 73 + 30 + 2 = 105. The 105/73 figures are used here; the apply.unito.it page still shows only the 30 non-EU-abroad figure. (b) Access classification: the en.unito.it degree-record summary box says 'Access: Local programmed', which contradicts both the admission call ('numero programmato a livello nazionale') and the descriptive text on the same page; this looks like a data-entry inconsistency in the UNITO course catalogue. (c) Non-EU deadline detail: the exact publication date and enrolment deadlines for the separate local UNITO ranking reserved to non-EU candidates residing abroad are not fixed in the call - the call and the supplementary notice both say they 'will be made known on the UniTo portal', so application_deadline_non_eu is marked uncertain for that final step even though the 9 September (test registration) and 11 September 2026 (Universitaly visa pre-enrolment + MyUniTo pre-enrolment) dates are firm. (d) The name of the official responsible for forming the non-EU ranking was corrected between the call (Prof. Marina Marchisio Conte) and the supplementary notice (Prof. Benedetta Bussolati, chair of the examining board) - the supplementary notice prevails. (e) Tuition: the EUR 156-2,800 range is the officially stated 2025-26 range; 2026-27 figures were not published in an English-language table that could be read directly, and depend on ISEE/financial situation, so they should be confirmed on the UNITO tuition-fees page. (f) The 'ALO' (Additional Learning Obligations) threshold wording differs between sources: the medinto.unito.it snippet mentions scores in Physics & Biology 25% below the highest score, while the en.unito.it degree record specifies a Physics & Mathematics section score below 4; this is a post-admission remediation matter, not an admission requirement, but the exact trigger could not be reconciled from live official pages.
